answers.note: I don't like any of these options. The home screen and the feature hub's reel door don't have to be tied together with this copy. Doesn't make a ton of sense since they're for different purposes. Don't love 'Roll credits on the group chat' for home close (readers have to think too much, but nice try) and none of these feel right for the actual card.

The reel is the core concept, then the screen introduces a key way it is used (play it on the big screen) and clips are a key takeaway (make your own clips). Your call on whether screen vs clips works best as second follow up, other goes third.

This was the closest option to what I'd like. However, rather than a still poster, we'll use a custom clipped short looped video that inspires a click on the play mark, which (unless you have a better idea) would be cool to launch a demo reel experience from. If that's a bad idea, we could play a demo reel housed in a modal that contextualizes what they're watching with some CTA.

While the left card is beautiful, the right side of this option could use a ton of redesign work around the reel presentation. The left card is beautiful for production, only needing shorter copy that reduces it to 2 lines max. too long now.

For a newer user, this is more all-encompassing, especially if they don't know about clips as a distinct side feature yet. Users who do know about clips will intuitively find that content under this broader category name.

notes.text: Round 2 decouples the thesis: the home's close and the hub's reel card each get their own plain lines, none a reader has to decode. The arc, his call handed to me: the reel, then the screen, then clips (the party, then the morning after). The poster becomes a short looped clip made by Partyreel's own creator from the demo album, and where its play mark leads is round 2's play ask (recommended: the demo's live reel over the page with one line of context and Start your event). The demo door keeps its look with its copy cut to two lines at most; the reel side beside it is round 2's wall ask.

answers.note: However, when we replaced the QR in the home hero with the album + QR, I didn't realize we were replacing every instance of the photos stacked behind a QR that pop out on hover with the album + QR too. It looks really silly here beside the 'Try the live demo...' CTA link. Would like something totally new here (or nothing at all beside the link), as well as swap back in the old version for the footer instance. The home hero version also needs a ton of work to feel more polished. Effectively, we're taking the 3 instances of its usage (home hero, here, footer) and handling each separately.
Could use a few better options though. The 'everyone's photos... live' and 'every new photo joins' from the other options also added value beyond this version's 'Your event', which is less clear.

The card side-by-side looks the cleanest, with each content being self-encapsulated. However, the motion in both cancels each other out, and I prefer the river. Maybe the reel card adds secondary info more statically (maybe a really cool bg image) rather than fighting the river demo card for attention.

We don't need to lean super hard into making our demo cohesive across every marketing surface when referenced. The demo is meant to be an experience within itself, but I'm disliking how much we're leaning on it specifically for all of our content as opposed to using more customized content at each point to really nail our goal. For example, an exciting intro/feature/reel video made for its own purpose in a section will always beat using a generic reel from a fake demo that our site visitors aren't auditing. If we're putting feature demos in front of them to understand the product, they don't care all the demos don't track back to one universal dataset. The contained player here keeps them in the marketing lane, rather than just dropping them off in an app demo without realizing, so the video may be framed contextually as needed.

This selection is far from perfect, just inspired a better idea: let's design the item so be a compact version of an event card, not text-heavy (if at all) but kind of showcasing multiple images in an album rather than 1 and a QR code, plus whatever other design touches you can think of. This hero sets the stage for the platform, and this item inherently is the core to that as the source of the photo stream. Want visitors to get an immediate impression of "oh, I make a shareable event and everyone uploads to it, cool!". The QR code alone feels limiting, like our product revolves around QRs-only rather than a "one link" concept, for which QRs are a huge contributor and key feature, but not defining. Reduces the idea of how easily this is to send a link in a group chat/email blast or simply write your custom link for people to copy/type.

I like this, feels a bit more subtle but still cool versus the guest row (which i considered heavily, but since this CTA section will often be followed by the footer, the guest row visual would be immediately followed by the footer's visual also pointing to the demo back-to-back, maybe that'd be great somewhere else). However, let's replace the 'A Partyreel production · partyreel.com' further down with this link so its a bit more spaced from the 'Start free' primary CTA button.
